title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The Haiku / Sonnet / Opus generation that followed Claude 3.5, running through 2025 and into 2026 with incremental point releases (Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7) that improved agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction-following precision without changing the naming scheme.

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

Anthropic described Opus 4.8 as "a modest but tangible improvement" over Opus 4.7, keeping pricing unchanged at $5/$25 per million input/output tokens. The gains were concentrated in a few areas:

- **Coding:** 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro (up from 64.3% on Opus 4.7); 88.6% on SWE-bench Verified.
- **Computer use / browser agents:** 84% on Online-Mind2Web — the strongest computer-use model at the time of release.
- **Honesty:** roughly 4x less likely than Opus 4.7 to fail to report flawed code it had written, part of a broader push on self-correction and honest reporting in long-running agentic evals.
- **Science:** narrowly led Humanity's Last Exam among frontier models.

Opus 4.8 remained the flagship Opus-tier model and is also the fallback model behind Fable 5's safety classifiers (see below).

---

## Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — a new "Mythos-class" tier (June 2026)

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic released **Claude Fable 5**, the first model in a new tier above Opus, internally called "Mythos-class." Anthropic called it state-of-the-art on nearly all tested capability benchmarks — software engineering, knowledge work, vision, and scientific research. Specs: 1M-token context window by default, up to 128K output tokens, priced at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.

Fable 5 shipped with the strongest safeguards Anthropic had applied to any model: on sensitive topics (mainly cybersecurity-adjacent tasks) queries are routed to Claude Opus 4.8 instead, tuned to trigger on under 5% of sessions.

**Export-control interruption:** three days after launch, on June 12, 2026, the US government applied export controls to Fable 5 and its sibling Mythos 5, restricting access for foreign nationals. After discussions with the government, Anthropic redeployed Fable 5 with additional cybersecurity classifiers, and the controls were lifted June 30 — Fable 5 became globally available again July 1, 2026 across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork.

Model ID: `claude-fable-5`.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

A landmark Sonnet release: Anthropic positioned it as closing most of the gap with Opus 4.8 at Sonnet pricing. On SWE-bench Pro, Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% versus 58.1% for Sonnet 4.6 and 69.2% for Opus 4.8; on knowledge work (GDPval-AA v2) Sonnet 5 actually edges out Opus 4.8 (1,618 vs 1,615).

**Notable changes from Sonnet 4.6:**
- **Native 1M-token context window** — the default and only context size (no smaller variant).
- **Adaptive thinking on by default** — requests without an explicit `thinking` field now think adaptively rather than not at all; manual extended thinking (`budget_tokens`) is removed and returns a 400 error, matching Opus 4.7/4.8.
- **New tokenizer** — the same text produces ~30% more tokens than under Sonnet 4.6, which affects token budgets and per-request cost even though per-token pricing is unchanged.
- **Fixed sampling parameters** — `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` can no longer be set to non-default values (400 error), pushing behavior steering toward the system prompt.
- **First Sonnet-tier model with real-time cybersecurity safeguards**, refusing prohibited/high-risk cybersecurity requests with `stop_reason: "refusal"`.

Pricing: $3/$15 per million input/output tokens (standard), with introductory pricing of $2/$10 in effect through August 31, 2026. Sonnet 5 became the default model for Free and Pro plans, and is available on Max, Team, and Enterprise. Model ID: `claude-sonnet-5`.

---

## Current Model Lineup (as of July 2026)

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest current-gen model |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Default for Free/Pro; near-Opus capability at Sonnet pricing |
| Opus 4.8 | `claude-opus-4-8` | Flagship Opus-tier; strongest coding/computer-use/science results below Mythos-class |
| Fable 5 | `claude-fable-5` | Mythos-class; Anthropic's most capable public model, 1M context, premium pricing |

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K tokens (stable Claude 2.1–4.x) → 1M tokens as the new default on Sonnet 5 and Fable 5
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → four tiers with the addition of Mythos-class (Fable 5) above Opus
- **Thinking:** Manual extended thinking (explicit token budgets) → adaptive thinking on by default, with budgets removed entirely on the newest models
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing — Sonnet 5 vs. Opus 4.8 is the clearest example yet
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems
- **Safety layering:** Frontier releases (Fable 5) now ship with automatic fallback routing to a less-restricted model tier rather than blanket refusals
